ns2:course.label: User Interface Design
ns2:course.description: A project-focused course that covers fundamental principles of user interface design, implementation, and evaluation. Small teams work on a semester-long project that includes: analysis of the problem domain, user skills, and tasks; iterative prototyping of interfaces to address user needs; conducting several forms of evaluation such as cognitive walkthroughs and usability tests; implementation of the final prototype. Non-technical majors may enroll in the course as non-programmers who participate in all aspects of the projects with the possible exception of implementation. Same as LIS 465. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 or 4 graduate hours. Prerequisite: CS 225 or CS 400.
